semester: 6th Semester (winter term start); 3rd Semester (summer term start)
prerequisites: School mathematics, e.g., derivatives of functions, equations with one and several variables, analytical geometry.

learning_outcomes.text: Students are able to classify the subfields of business administration.
describe essential links between commercial aspects and technical areas of companies.
propose solutions to business problems by selecting appropriate operational production factors.
assess the choice of legal form and location.
apply business administration methods to problems in corporate divisions.
use business administration criteria as a basis for decision-making.
understand accounting and annual financial statements in companies, and perform cost and performance accounting in practical examples.
analyze and assess the relationships of production and cost theory, as well as long-term and short-term production planning.
relate aspects of information procurement in the sales area and sales policy instruments to each other.
compare dynamic and static investment appraisal methods and use them to solve tasks in the financial sector.

syllabus_topics: Subject, methods, and history of Business Administration
Structure of the company including operational production factors (dispositive and elementary)
Choice of legal form and location
Accounting, annual financial statements, cost and performance accounting
Production and cost theory as well as long-term and short-term production planning
Information procurement in the sales area and sales policy instruments
Dynamic and static methods of investment appraisal
assessment_rules: Credit points are awarded upon successful completion of the module exam. A prerequisite for participation in the exam is successful participation in the exercises. The grade's weight for the final grade is determined by the credit points.
